idiom_name: module-level function taking the serviced object (duck-typed); Object.assign trait object as the member-syntax alternative
implementation_notes: JavaScript functions are already free of classes, so the servant is normally a module-scope function that takes the serviced object - moveTo(shape, position) - with duck typing standing in for the capability interface (the function simply requires the properties it uses). When the behaviour should read as a member, the language's option is a trait object copied onto the serviced prototype with Object.assign or a mixin class expression; modern guidance treats that as a last resort because the methods shadow existing prototype members, leave no trace on the class, and are invisible to static analysis. The classic servant class has no place here: it would only duplicate what a function already provides - keep an object only when the behaviour carries configuration that would otherwise become module-level mutable state, or when it must be swapped per scenario.
pitfalls: Object.assign onto a prototype silently overwrites same-named members, applies to every instance and subclass, and is a last-writer-wins race between libraries - tools and linters cannot see the installed methods.

Methods copied as plain functions depend on call-site this: passing shape.moveTo as a callback loses the receiver and throws, which is one more reason to prefer a function servant that takes the object explicitly.
Duck typing defers the contract to runtime: a servant that assumes shape.position fails somewhere inside the call, so validate at the boundary or document the required shape.
sources: MDN, Object.assign() - copies enumerable own properties onto a target, the mechanism behind trait-object mixins (and why accessors and prototype merging need care); https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Object/assign
MDN, Classes - class syntax, prototypes and methods, the surface a prototype mixin patches; https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Classes

patterns.dev, Mixin Pattern - recommends composition or small utility modules over mixins for most modern cases and lists the shadowing/visibility costs; https://www.patterns.dev/vanilla/mixin-pattern/
